_comment: WHERE THE PROGRAMME ACTUALLY IS. `docs/reshape-plan.md` is 800 lines of narrative with each step's status embedded in four different tables, and the status is what drifts: 2.1 (B2) merged as PR #189 on 2026-08-20 and the row naming it as NEXT still read 'never started' three days and six merged slices later, which is how it came within one instruction of being built twice. This file is the status of record; the STATUS INDEX in the plan is rendered from it, and `tests/test_plan_state.py` makes the TREE adjudicate every row.
_artifact: The one path (or `path::token`) whose presence means the step has shipped. `done` requires it present; `pending`/`held` requires it ABSENT — that second direction is the one that failed here, and it is the whole reason the field exists. THREE artifacts are FORWARD-DECLARED (0.5, 0.6, 0.7) because the plan names no file for them: if the slice that lands one picks a different name, the absent-direction stays quiet, and the DONE direction is what catches it when somebody flips the status. Say what you built; do not flip a status without its artifact.

steps.title: B5 — the Odoo half of the baseline
steps.note:
WAITS ON R4.27 DIRECTLY. It was filed as waiting on correctness-plan D6, and **D6 was REFUTED at 0.139.0 by its own mandated measurement** (R4.111): the gate is correct at both branches and the defect is upstream in the marking. So the cheap route to an Odoo baseline is closed, and what remains is R4.27 -- the population D0 is blocked over, and a far larger item. Odoo measured mean 0.181, std 0.203 over three reps. A further signal says fixing R4.27 alone may not be enough: one gate refusal was itself a locator-ambiguity failure, so there may be a second independent Odoo problem underneath. `pending` rather than `held` because R4.27 is a register finding, not a row in this table. **SURVEYED at 0.140.0** (`docs/reads-over-post.md`, decision D7): eleven approaches to R4.27, six dead. The lead is a body-evidence read allowlist, and it is NOT scheduled — the assumption that fixing the marking unblocks Odoo is measured by nothing, and six free measurements settle it. Run measurement #1 before treating this step as costed. **AND THE MEASUREMENT CAME BACK NO (R4.114, 0.141.0).** Flipping the wire marks off does NOT make an Odoo replay green -- the gate refusal becomes a LOCATOR refusal on the same step, which never bound in either arm; and a census of the three-rep series finds 4 of 18 non-passing rows already failing on locators with no mark involved, plus 6 that never produced a recipe at all. So **this step is NOT blocked on R4.27**, which was the working assumption. It is blocked on locator ambiguity on a generated DOM, and partly on discovery. Do not cost it as a marking fix. **AND AT 0.142.0 THE BLOCKER CHANGED IDENTITY A THIRD TIME (R4.115).** R4.114 said locator ambiguity; measured, the locator binds uniquely on the FIRST candidate once the page has RENDERED, and what the replay reads is a shell -- `thead th` 0, `body_chars` 3. Odoo serves 5 elements at `domcontentloaded` and settles at 0.62-1.08 s, on 7 of 7 scenarios; Gitea is complete at `domcontentloaded` on 7 of 7. So this step is blocked on a READINESS RACE at three sites, with R4.27 deciding only whether a raced step can HEAL. **Do not cost it as a marking fix and do not cost it as a locator fix.** Note also that the obvious readiness remedy is already REFUTED (a retry on `resolve() -> None` re-drives four safety refusals and was measured binding a wrong record), so this is not a small step -- it needs a new sensor class, which is D5's bar. **AND AT 0.143.0 THE PICTURE RESOLVED INTO THREE LEGS, ONE OF WHICH IS NOW MEASURED TO BE SUFFICIENT WHEN COMBINED (R4.117).** The marking fix and the readiness fix each fail ALONE on a fresh Odoo recipe and TOGETHER complete it -- so 2.4b is blocked on BOTH, not either. The third leg is upstream of both: R4.118, the learn thrashing on navigation and caching 100%-`navigate` recipes (4 of 5 learns degraded), which no replay-side fix touches. **Order them learn-capture -> readiness -> marking**: the first is upstream of recipe variance and the cheapest, and until it lands, any measurement of the other two is taken over recipes that vary run to run. **THE THREE LEGS ABOVE HAVE ALL LANDED, AND THIS NOTE WAS FIVE SLICES STALE UNTIL 0.161.0.** learn-capture is R4.118, FIXED at 0.147.0 and validated on the OUTCOME (two degenerate recipes became healthy, the control stayed healthy); readiness is R4.115, whose replay-resolve site closed at 0.148.0 and whose two GATE sites closed at 0.158.0 -- the entry was marked `fixed` with two of its three named sites still open, which is how it survived; marking is D7, built at 0.150.0 and adjudicated at 0.151.0 (the JSON-RPC half; GraphQL, R4.27's original 12/12 population, is untouched). Measured across those: Odoo availability **0.181 -> 0.524**, `varies` **5 -> 0**, and `over_gated/drift` **4 -> 0** across 21 scenario-observations. Reading this note before that sentence existed would have sent someone to fix three things that are done -- the B2 failure exactly, one table over.

**WHAT BLOCKS 2.4b NOW IS A DIFFERENT SET, AND THE CEILING IS ARITHMETIC.** Only FOUR of seven Odoo rows can currently pass, so the ceiling is **4/7 = 0.571** and two passes of three have reached it exactly. The three holds are: **R4.111** (both writes at 0.000, on `unique=True` failing to bind on a generated DOM -- 2 rows), **R4.130** (`odoo-search` answers off the landing page with zero actions, so it scores `no_actions_needed`, a permanent 0 that is NOT a product failure -- 1 row; its own entry records that the blocker it named was WRONG and that the real one, R4.131, is fixed, so whether it is now repairable needs one paid run), and **R4.140** (a ~1/3 `shape_drift` flake on `odoo-filter-status`, goal-shape specific and measured NOT to generalise). **Do not cost this step as a readiness fix, a locator fix or a marking fix** -- all three identities are spent.

**AND A PRIOR QUESTION THIS STEP SHOULD SETTLE BEFORE IT CUTS A BASELINE (R4.141, 0.161.0)**: every corpus READ replays with `llm_calls=1`, measured on both substrates, because no read is pinned. Pinning cannot fix it here -- 0 of 10 reads are pinnable, Odoo carrying no `id` or `data-testid` on any of 765 leaf text holders. So an Odoo (or Gitea) `availability_rate` counts rows that call the model on every replay, and the number does not say which. That is a question about what the baseline MEANS, not a blocker on cutting one.
